papers.title: Venomics AI: a computational exploration of global venoms for antibiotic discovery
A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization.

models.architecture_or_algorithm: deep learning model combining a peptide-sequence encoder with neural networks for antimicrobial activity prediction (MIC prediction)
models.candidate_reason: APEX is a deep learning model for AMP prediction (MIC). Used in a large-scale venom peptide screen, but code and data not available.
blocking_issues: Code and trained model not publicly available
models.representative_reason: APEX is a recent deep learning model for AMP MIC prediction, used in a high-profile venom study. If code/weights become available, it could serve as a representative DL sequence model for AMP classification.

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Transformer variational autoencoder (VAE) combined with Bayesian optimization (BO) and APEX predictor for antimicrobial activity optimization
models.dataset_source_or_link: not_reported_in_available_evidence (VAE training data not specified, APEX in-house)
models.candidate_reason: ApexGO is a generative AI model for AMP optimization, combining VAE and BO. Could benchmark AMP sequence optimization tasks.
blocking_issues: Code and model not publicly available
models.representative_reason: ApexGO is a novel generative model for AMP optimization with strong experimental validation. If weights are released, it could represent generative AMP design models.

datasets.dataset_source: Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides

model_dataset_links.relationship: DBAASP used as reference AMP database, likely for benchmarking or training support.
ConoServer used as source of venom proteins for generating VEPs.
ArachnoServer used as source of spider proteins for generating VEPs.
ISOB used as source of snake proteins for generating VEPs.
VenomZone used as source of venom proteins from six taxa for generating VEPs.
ApexGO relies on APEX predictor; training data for VAE not specified, APEX training data is in-house and not publicly described.

metrics.usage: Proportion of predicted peptides showing antimicrobial activity in vitro
metrics.evidence: 53 out of 58 synthesized VEPs (91.4%) exhibited activity against at least one pathogenic strain.

metrics.usage: Percentage of ApexGO-optimized peptides with enhanced antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative pathogens
metrics.evidence: ApexGO achieved an 85% ground-truth experimental hit rate and a 72% success rate in enhancing antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative pathogens.

important_evidence: APEX deep learning model predicted MIC values for venom-encrypted peptides, achieving 91.4% hit rate in vitro.
ApexGO generative model optimized peptides with 85% experimental hit rate and 72% success rate against Gram-negative pathogens.
Both models lack publicly available code and weights.
Training data for APEX is in-house and not publicly accessible.
uncertainties: Code and trained weights for APEX and ApexGO are not available.
APEX training data (in-house peptides) not publicly described.
ApexGO VAE training data details missing.
DBAASP database URL not provided in evidence.
